title: Wang Chuqin out of WTT Champions Montpellier with injury
standfirst: The world champion's withdrawal leaves Lin Shidong to lead China's men at the singles-only event, which starts on Tuesday. Sun Yingsha returns at the head of a six-strong women's squad.
body: Wang Chuqin has pulled out of WTT Champions Montpellier with an injury. Reports in China differ on who has taken his place in the men's draw for the tournament, which runs from 27 October to 1 November at the Sud de France Arena.

His withdrawal leaves Lin Shidong at the head of a five-man Chinese entry with Wen Ruibo, Zhou Qihao, Xiang Peng and Liang Jingkun. Sun Yingsha leads the women's squad, which also includes Wang Manyu, Kuai Man, Wang Yidi, Chen Xingtong and Chen Yi, who won the Asian singles title on Sunday.

For the home crowd the focus is on Félix and Alexis Lebrun. Félix, the European champion, is the world No 2 and Alexis is No 8. Japan's Sora Matsushima, the world No 1, returns after reaching last year's final, and Flavien Coton and Thibault Poret are also in the French entry.
Wang Manyu arrives as world No 1 again after regaining the top spot in the 12 October rankings, and Wang Yidi defends the women's title. Prithika Pavade and Jia Nan Yuan lead the French women.
WTT Champions events are singles only and straight knockout, so one defeat ends a player's tournament. Points here also count towards qualification for December's WTT Finals Hong Kong.

Play runs in two sessions a day, at midday and in the evening local time. The finals are on Sunday 1 November, with sessions at 11am and 5.30pm in Montpellier, an hour ahead of the UK. This is the third edition of the event in the city.
author: michael
